# trace-thread

> Links a payment's legs across rails using UETR, Fedwire IMAD/OMAD, end-to-end and transaction IDs, ACH trace numbers and stablecoin issuer references, marks where the identifier trail breaks, and tests recall and hold policies on a taint model. Engineering checklist, not legal advice.

Standard library only, no network calls. Identifier links (UETR, IMAD, transaction hash, returns and recalls naming the original) are kept apart from inferred pass-through and split links, which are capped below every identifier link. The simulator replays a case under FIFO, LIFO, haircut or bounding taint rules and compares notice and hold scenarios. It is a policy-testing model: nothing in today's networks propagates a fraud flag by itself. Tested on synthetic data only.

Built and maintained by Art Akopian, CEO of Banrox (https://banrox.com).

## Docs

- [SKILL.md](https://github.com/BanroxArt/trace-thread/blob/main/SKILL.md): Agent skill for building and reading a case.

## Source

- [link.py](https://github.com/BanroxArt/trace-thread/blob/main/src/tracethread/link.py): Identifier and inferred links, threads.
- [taint.py](https://github.com/BanroxArt/trace-thread/blob/main/src/tracethread/taint.py): Taint accounting and the recall and hold model.
- [ids.py](https://github.com/BanroxArt/trace-thread/blob/main/src/tracethread/ids.py): Identifier formats.

## Optional

- [examples/case.json](https://github.com/BanroxArt/trace-thread/blob/main/examples/case.json): A synthetic case from a changed invoice to a stablecoin deposit.
